items.title: 카카오페이증권, 인수업 인가 후 첫 스팩 설립…IB 사업 본격화

items.title: 증설, 또 증설... 이수페타시스, 7공장 투자협약

items.title: 장덕현 삼성전기 사장 "MLCC와 기판 유례없는 대형 성장 기회"

items.title: 'CNT 5000톤' 장담하더니…제이오, 증설 중단

items.title: 이엔에프테크놀로지, 美카일 공장 삼성 인텔 이어 세 번째 고객 확보

items.title: AMD, 아드레날린 26.10.2 버전 출시...시스템 종료 현상 수정
items.snippet: AMD가 '아드레날린 에디션' 26.10.2 선택형 버전을 출시했다고 2일 밝혔다.아드레날린 에디션은 AMD의 그래픽 드라이버 소프트웨어다. 이번 버전은 게임 실행 오류와 시스템 강제 종료 현상을 고쳤다.RDNA3 아키텍처 기반 라데온 RX 7600 시리즈에서 게임 '발로 모티스'를 실행하면 간헐적으로 시스템이 꺼지던 문제를 해결했다. 라데온 RX 7000 시리즈 전반에서 나던 타임아웃 오류도 잡았다. 그래픽 처리 응답이 늦어져 드라이버 연결이 끊기는 현상이다.성능 지표 오버레이를 켠 상태에서 다른 창을 여닫으면 앱이 꺼지거나 드라

items.title: 코아시아세미, 삼성 파운드리 4나노 반도체 출하 시작
items.snippet: 반도체 디자인하우스(DSP) 코아시아세미가 삼성전자 파운드리 4나노(nm) 공정 기반 반도체 소자(디바이스) 웨이퍼의 양산 출하를 시작했다고 2일 밝혔다.해당 웨이퍼에 형성된 소자는 고성능 연산(HPC) 환경에서 고속 데이터 전송, 처리를 돕는 네트워크 스위치 칩이다. 칩 면적은 800mm² 이상이다. 코아시아세미가 수행한 프로젝트 중 가장 면적이 넓은 빅다이다.단일 칩 면적이 넓을 수록 수율 관리가 어렵다. 제품에 불량이 섞이 확률이 높아지기 때문이다. 전력 소모와 열 발생 등 설계 과정에서 고려할 변수도 많아 제작 난도가 높다.

items.title: 포스코홀딩스, 2.5조 자금 확보액 중 10% "연내 자사주 매입·소각"

items.title: 이재용 삼성전자 회장, 日 첨단 패키징 연구거점 방문
items.snippet: 이재용 삼성전자 회장이 일본 첨단 반도체 패키징 연구거점 '어드밴스트 패키지 랩(APL)'을 1일 방문했다. 공식 개소 후 두 달 만에 처음으로 현장 점검에 나섰다. items.title: 삼성전자, 2030년 8인치 파운드리 완전 철수
items.snippet: 삼성전자가 8인치 파운드리 사업에서 완전히 철수하기로 방침을 정하고 고객사들에 이 같은 계획을 통보한 것으로 확인됐다. 삼성전자는 그동안 8인치 생산라인을 단계적으로 축소하겠다고만 밝혀왔다. 종료 시점을 못 박은 것은 처음이다. 삼성전자에 반도체 생산을 맡겨 온 국내 반도체 팹리스 업체들은 대체 생산처 확보에 비상이 걸렸다.2일 업계에 따르면 삼성전자는 최근 8인치 파운드리 고객사들에 2030년 말까지 관련 생산라인 가동을 모두 종료하겠다는 계획을 통보했다. 8인치 사업을 정리하고 12인치 웨이퍼 기반의 미세공정에 인력과 설비 투자

items.title: 애경산업, 3분기 영업적자 33억원…전년비 적자 전환

items.title: 현대차 10월 판매 6.3%↓·기아 10.3%↑…기아 내수 27.5% 급증

items.snippet: 한화오션이 잠수함에서 어뢰 등 무기를 바다로 밀어 발사하는 장비인 ‘수평발사장치’를 국산화하는 데 성공했다.1일 한화오션은 국방과학연구소와 함께 10년간의 개발 끝에 잠수함의 핵심 장비인 ‘수평발사장치’ 독자 개발에 성공했다고 밝혔다. 수평발사장치는 잠수함 안에 실려 있는 수중 폭발 무기인 어뢰를 바다로 밀어내는 장치다. 그간 수입에 의존해왔던 이 장비를 국산화함에 따라 이 회사는 비용 절감, 납기 단축 등 효과를 기대하고 있다.이번에 개발된 장치는 ‘워터램’ 방식을 취하고 있다. 주사기 피스톤처럼 물의 압력을 이용해 어뢰를 수평으로 밀어내는 식이다. 이때 어뢰가 정해진 속도로 안전하게 빠져나갈 수 있도록 물이 밀어내는 힘을 정밀하게 조절하는 게 관건이다. 한화오션은 이처럼 안정적으로 발사를 제어하는 핵심 기술을 완성했다고 설명했다. 발사관의...

items.snippet: LG전자가 광고 기반 무료 스트리밍(FAST) 서비스 'LG채널'을 베트남에 출시했다. 동남아에서도 TV 판매에 머물지 않고 콘텐츠·광고 플랫폼으로 수익원을 넓히는 전략이다. LG전자 베트남법인은 29일 LG채널을 현지에 정식 출시했다. 웹OS 스마트TV 이용자는 구독료나 셋톱박스 없이 다양한 프로그램을 시청할 수 있다. 시청자는 무료로 콘텐츠를 보고, LG전자는 프로그램 사이에 붙는 광고로 수익을 낸다. 콘텐츠는 현지 방송사 중심으로 꾸렸다.

items.title: 李, 내일 ‘내년 정부 예산안’ 시정연설…국회 협조 요청할 듯
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 오는 2일 내년도 예산안 시정연설을 한다고 강유정 청와대 수석대변인이 1일 밝혔다. 이 대통령은 당일 정부가 제출한 2027년도 예산안의 편성 방향과 주요 내용을 설명할 예정이다.정부가 국회에 제출한 내년도 예산안은 총지출 기준 820조9000억원으로, 올해 본예산(727조9000억원)보다 12.8% 증가했다. 역대 최대 규모이자 역대 최고 증가율이다.예산안에는 미래 성장동력 확보와 민생 안정, 지방 주도 성장 등을 위한 재정 투자가 담겼다. 특히 162조원 규모의 미래대응기금 신설이 주요 쟁점으로 꼽힌다.이 대통령은 민생 안정과 미래 성장동력 확보를 위한 예산안의 필요성을 강조하고, 국회에 조속한 심의와 처리를 당부할 것으로 예상된다.[서울=뉴시스]

items.title: 넋놓고 지켜본 바이낸스 임원들…北, 20분만에 8조원 털어갔다
items.snippet: 가상자산 업계를 공황 속으로 밀어 넣은 최악의 사이버 침해 사태가 바이낸스를 덮쳤다. 북한의 국가 지원 해킹 조직이 단 20분 만에 최소 63억 달러(약 8조 4000억 원)에 달하는 디지털 자산을 약탈해 갔고 바이낸스 직원들은 넋 놓고 실시간으로 자금이 빠져나가는 장면을 지켜볼 수 밖에 없었다. 업계에선 이번 해킹 사건이 가상자산 업계에 큰 위기를 초래할 수 있다고 보고 있다. 디지털 자산이 전통 금융을 대체할 안전한 자산이 될 수 있는지에 대한 근본적인 의구심이 다시 수면 위로 올라왔기 때문이다. 월스트리트저널과 로이터 등 외신에 따르면 해킹이 일어났던 29일(현지시간) 당시 아랍에미리트(UAE) 아부다비에 위치한 바이낸스 보안팀 모니터에 경고등이 켜졌다. 거래소 내부 지갑에서 10억 달러가 넘는 자금이 무단 유출되는 정황이 포착된 것이다...

items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. By measuring the transmitted probe electric field as a function of pump-probe delay, we directly retrieve the pump-induced phase shift an...

items.snippet: 30일 낮 12시쯤 인천국제공항 제1터미널에서 출항하는 중국남방항공·중국동방항공·중국국제항공(에어차이나) 등 중국 항공사 3곳의 발권 시스템에 오류가 발생하면서, 항공권 발권 업무가 5시간가량 중단됐다. 이에 탑승 수속을 일일이 수기로 진행하면서 중국 상하이, 광저우, 칭다오 등으로 향하는 항공기 38편이 지연됐다. 승객 1200여 명이 불편을 겪은 것으로 알려졌다. 사진은 인천공항 제1터미널 체크인 카운터에서 출국하려는 사람들이 대기하는 모습.

items.title: 내년 장기요양보험료 세대당 月1100원 올라
items.snippet: 내년도 장기요양보험료가 가입 세대당 월평균 1100원 오른다. 보험료율 인상 폭이 2021년도 이후 6년 만에 가장 크다. 장기요양보험은 고령이나 질병 등으로 혼자 일상생활을 하기 어려운 노인에게 방문 요양비나 요양시설 이용비 등을 지원하는 제도로, 이 보험료는 건강보험 가입자 모두가 부과 대상이다. 보건복지부는 30일 장기요양위원회에서 내년도 장기요양보험료율을 올해보다 0.76%포인트 높은 건보료의 13.9%로 결정했다고 밝혔다. 이에 따라 세대당 월평균 장기요양보험료는 1만9029원에서 2만129원으로 오른다. 건보료를 매달 10만원 내는 가입자라면, 장기요양보험료로 1만3900원이 부과되는 것이다.

items.title: 부산, 아기 울음소리 7년 만에 가장 컸다
items.snippet: 지난 7월 부산에서 태어난 아이는 1365명으로 2019년 7월 이후 가장 많았다. 1년 전보다 144명(11.8%) 늘었다. 올 1~7월 출생아는 9388명으로 지난해 같은 기간보다 15.2% 늘었다. 부산시는 출산·육아 지원을 확대해 이런 증가세를 이어가겠다는 계획이다. 부산시는 올해 추가경정예산을 통해 산후조리비와 산모·신생아 건강관리 서비스 지원 대상을 각각 2000명 늘리기로 했다. 아이 한 명당 산후조리비를 최대 100만원 지원한다. 산후조리원 이용료와 병원 진료비 등으로 쓸 수 있다. 산모·신생아 건강관리 서비스는 전문 교육을 받은 관리사가 출산 가정을 찾아가 산모의 회복을 돕고 신생아를 돌봐주는 제도다.

items.title: 야간버스 모는 아빠 “가족은 내가 돌아갈 종점”
items.snippet: “가족은 버스 기사인 제가 운행을 마치고 돌아가는 종점이자, 내일을 살게 해주는 힘입니다.”(‘31초 영상제’ 최우수상 박용기씨)

items.title: “암 환자도 이젠 집에서 치료해야… 환자도 병원도 모두 만족할 수 있어”
items.snippet: “이제 병원들도 재택 의료에 우선순위를 둬야 합니다. 환자는 물론이고, 병원 입장에서도 이를 통해 얻는 것이 많습니다.” 스웨덴 살그렌스카 대학병원의 부부 할베리(Boubou Hallberg) 원장은 지난 20일 본지 인터뷰에서 우리나라가 확대하려는 ‘방문 진료’ 관련 질문이 나오자, 이같이 답했다. 서울에서 열린 국제병원연맹 ‘세계 병원 대회’(20~22일) 참석차 방한한 할베리 원장은 스웨덴 내 최대 규모(약 1600병상에 직원 1만8000명 근무) 병원을 이끌면서도, 방문 진료와 유사한 ‘재택 의료’의 자국 내 확산을 위해 앞장서온 의료인으로 통한다.

items.title: 25년간 매일 ‘아침 편지’… “400만명 지친 마음 보듬었죠”
items.snippet: “400만 명에게 보내는 편지가 아닙니다. 단 한 사람에게 쓴 편지가 매일 아침 그만큼의 집에 도착하는 것입니다.” 지난 20일 충북 충주시 ‘깊은산속 옹달샘’ 집필실에서 만난 고도원(75) 아침편지문화재단 이사장은 25년간 편지를 이어 온 힘을 이렇게 설명했다. 아침편지문화재단은 29일 ‘제13회 21세기 인문가치포럼’ 개막식에서 ‘2026 인문가치대상’ 단체 부문 상을 받았다. 25년간 좋은 글을 무료로 전하고 그 울림을 명상과 나눔으로 확장한 공로다.

items.title: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ Spin-1/2 Qubits
items.abstract: Scaling silicon spin qubits to fault-tolerant processors requires semiconductor foundry integration, yet it remains unclear how industrial fabrication and dense device integration affect qubit control and noise. Here we study ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ electron spin-1/2 qubits fabricated using Intel's industry-compatible 300 mm process and incorporating micromagnets for electrically driven spin resonance, using a high-performance device fabricated in the RIKEN research cleanroom as a reference. Primitive $π/2$-gate fidelities reach the 99.99% level in the Intel devices, which also exhibit longer idle coherence, weaker low-frequency correlations and reduced qubit-to-qubit variability across several measured characteristics. items.snippet: 이번 국정감사에서 의료계 최대 이슈는 9월 30일 있었던 아주대 소아응급센터 압수수색. 생후 4개월 아기가 외래진료 중 호흡곤란 등의 증세를 보여 소아응급센터로 옮겨져 응급 처치를 받다가 사망했는데, 이로 인해 해당 병원 의사들이 범죄자 취급을 받은 건 그냥 넘어가서는 안 될 일이 맞다. 하지만 위 사건에 묻혀 조명되지 않은 건이 하나 더 있었으니, 그건 10월 7일 나온, 더불어민주당 송영길 의원의 발언이었다. 그는 국군의무사령관에게 군의관이 감소하고 있는 것에 대한 대책을 묻던 중 다음과 같이 말한다. “군 의사 같은 경우는 전쟁 상황이라는 특수 상황에서 전문의의 고도의 의학지식이 필요한 건 아니잖아요.” 이 말만으로도 납득이 어렵지만, 그가 내놓은 해법은 더 충격이었다. “긴급하게 응급적으로 처리할 수 있는 PA(Physician Ass...

items.title: 분식집에서 사라진 김밥… 파인다이닝 주연으로
items.snippet: 흑백요리사 2에 ‘서울 엄마’로 출연한 우정욱 셰프가 한글과 영어로 된 김밥 요리책 ‘김밥 책’을 최근 냈다. 출판 기념회에는 국내 유일 미쉐린 3스타 레스토랑 ‘밍글스’ 강민구 오너 셰프를 비롯해 국내 정상급 셰프·외식업계 관계자 150여 명이 참석했다. 예상보다 많이 모였다. 우 셰프는 “(자신의 식당) ‘수퍼판’을 찾는 외국 손님들로부터 ‘김밥 마는 법 알려주는 요리책을 내달라’는 요청을 많이 받았다”고 했다.

items.title: 여덟 가지 아름다운 경치를 표현한 산수화
items.snippet: 소상팔경도(瀟湘八景圖)는 중국 동정호(洞庭湖) 주변 소수(瀟水)와 상수(湘水) 유역의 여덟 가지 아름다운 경치를 그린 그림이다. 그 전통의 시작은 중국 북송으로 거슬러 올라간다. 11세기 문인 관료인 송적(宋迪)의 득의작(得意作·작가가 뜻한 바를 잘 구현한 작품)으로 평사낙안(平沙落雁), 원포귀범(遠浦歸帆), 산시청람(山市晴嵐), 강천모설(江天暮雪), 동정추월(洞庭秋月), 소상야우(瀟湘夜雨), 연사모종(煙寺暮鐘), 어촌석조(漁村夕照)가 있고 이를 팔경(八景)이라 했다는 기록이 전한다.

items.title: “등산할 때 친목은 사절, 버스만 예약할게요”
items.snippet: 서울에 사는 디자이너 박모(39·여)씨는 최근 혼자 당일치기로 설악산 등산을 다녀왔다. 등산 버스 모바일 앱에서 5만원대 왕복 차편을 예약했다.

items.title: “해외에서 엄마 김치 먹고 싶은 분?”… 시골 우체국이 살아남는 법
items.snippet: ‘백수’ 우체국이 새 일자리를 찾았다. 전남광주 영광군 백수읍에 있는 우체국 이야기다. 이 우체국은 인구 감소로 우편물이 줄어 새로운 활로가 절실한 상황이었다. 눈을 해외로 돌렸다. 김장철인 지난해 12월, SNS에 ‘엄마 김치가 그리운 해외 교민들의 김치 배송을 돕겠다’는 글을 올렸다. 이른바 ‘김치 해외 배송 대행’이다. 과정은 이렇다. 백수우체국에 신청하면 집으로 김치를 담을 수 있는 금속 용기(캔)를 보내준다. 여기에 김치를 담아 백수우체국으로 보내면 된다. 나머지는 우체국 직원들이 알아서 한다. 김치캔을 보랭 상자에 넣고 산소·발효 가스 흡수제와 보랭 팩 등을 추가해 재포장한 뒤 국제특급우편(EMS)으로 원하는 해외 주소에 발송해 준다. 소비자는 EMS 요금만 내면 된다.

items.title: 8만원어치 주문, 지출은 0원… 이게 된다고?
items.snippet: 크리스피 반반치킨에 치즈볼 5개, 탕수육(대)과 마라탕, 아이스 아메리카노에 딸기 생크림 케이크까지. 먹고 싶은 음식을 배달앱 장바구니에 담았더니 총 8만2700원어치다. 빠르게 배달해 준다는 ‘토끼배달’을 선택하자 기본 배달비 4000원에 추가금 1000원이 붙었다. 결제 버튼을 누르자 순식간에 매장에서 주문을 확인했다는 알림이 뜨고, 지도 위로 배달원의 위치가 움직이기 시작했다. 잠시 뒤 ‘배달 완료!’라는 안내가 떴다. 영수증에는 ‘이번 주문으로 아낀 금액 8만7700원, 4380kcal 아끼셨어요!!’라는 문구가 적혀 있었다. 하지만 실제로 배달된 음식은 하나도 없었다. 빠져나간 돈도 0원이다. 가짜 배달앱 ‘음식만안와요’에서 주문했기 때문이다.

items.title: 노벨상까지 받은 분자 연구, 왜 과학자들은 재앙을 걱정할까
items.snippet: 그리스 신화에서 잘생긴 외모로 유명한 나르키소스는 다른 사람의 말을 메아리처럼 반복하는 요정 에코의 사랑을 거절했다가 자신과 사랑에 빠지는 저주를 받았다. 그는 거울처럼 맑은 샘물에 비친 자신만 바라보다가 죽어 자기도취를 뜻하는 나르시시즘이란 말이 생겼다. 그의 얼굴은 그지없이 아름다웠지만, 거울을 보듯 마주한 자기 모습은 삶의 의지를 빼앗을 뿐이었다.

items.title: 연락 두절에 재판도 불출석… ‘먹튀 변호사’에 우는 의뢰인들

items.title: 의사가 된 ‘톤즈의 아이’... “이태석 신부의 길 걷습니다”

items.snippet: 혼슈 북단, ‘기타도호쿠(北東北) 3현’으로 불리는 아오모리·이와테·아키타현은 일본의 오지로 불리는 곳이다. 일본인조차 평생 이곳을 밟아보지 못하고 죽는 사람이 적지 않다고 할 만큼 산도 깊고, 물도 깊다. ‘비탕(秘湯)’, ‘탕치(湯治)’란 말도 이곳을 여행하며 처음 들었다. 사람 손길이 거의 닿지 않은 ‘숨겨진 온천’이란 뜻으로, 병이 치유될 만큼 몸에 좋은 성분이 다량으로 함유된 온천이 많다고 했다. ‘일본 온천여행’을 펴낸 박성희 인페인터글로벌 대표는 “기타도호쿠 지역의 명탕(名湯)들은 활화산 수맥에서 솟아나는 자연수로 기준치를 뛰어넘는 유황과 염화물 성분을 품은 것은 물론 용출량이 풍부해 원천수를 여과 없이 욕조로 흘려보내는 ‘가케나가시’ 방식을 유지한다”고 했다.

items.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

items.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. items.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. items.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. items.title: 10 kV $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
items.abstract: $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
items.abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. items.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification
items.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a complex, multi-step process that requires both high precision and low operating costs. Therefore, detecting defects in a high-volume setting is an important component of wafer map analysis for reliable production. However, most state-of-the-art deep learning approaches require a full scan of the surface, which hinders the development of high-throughput inspection systems. items.abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a...

items.title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering
items.abstract: Controlling the number n of connected octahedra layers in two-dimensional metal halide perovskites enables fine control of the semiconductor band gap that is highly advantageous for optoelectronic and light emission applications. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. items.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
items.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. During the growth of the shell, the wurtzite structure of the core is replicated in the shell, without any creation of defects. This is true for a wide range of shell thickness, from about one monolayer, up to 25 nm thanks to the good lattice match between the InAs material of the core and the ZnTe material of the shell. While (1 100) m-facets and (11 20) a-facets coexist on the sidewalls of the core, during the growth of the ZnTe shell the size of the m-facets progressively increases at the expense of the a-facets which eventually disappear. items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. The technique enhances OTA gain by compensating for its finite output conductance using a cross-coupled transistor pair, with an on-chip calibration loop that eliminates the need for a replica circuit or external tuning. The calibration routine increases the gain by driving the steady state error of the OTA in a unity gain feedback loop toward zero. The implementation addresses practical challenges involving comparator offset, DAC design, and subtractor gain and offset. items.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
items.abstract: Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools. First, the designer teaches the agent the gm/ID method: map the specifications to transconductances and minimum currents, choose gm/ID per device role from characterized lookup tables, and size from equations, leaving a few knobs to search and an explainable design. Second, the agent learns the gLayout framework and taught layout practice, and writes a reusable layout generator that closes the layout and extraction loop at designer-approved gates. items.title: When Does Heterogeneity Pay Off? Understanding GPU-WSE System Complementarity
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Colossal magnetoresistance in narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$
items.abstract: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. items.title: Volumetric Nanophotonics for Enhanced Scintillation and Remote Light Outcoupling
items.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. items.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. items.title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. items.title: Parity-Resolved Many-Body Kinetics of a Topological Qubit under Nonequilibrium Phonon Pulses
items.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,μ\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75--1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. items.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). To address these, we present four synthesizable peripheral blocks: a Flush-Merge Enable (FME) controller, a Confidence-Based Early-Exit (EE) module, a Precision Register with Decoder (PR/PD), and a Bit-Serial Cycle Controller (CC), co-designed to minimize switching activity, wordline overhead, and leakage. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 μm2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 μm2 post-PnR. items.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning
items.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. In such domains, frontier models tend to give generic answers. Knowledge graphs (KGs) can ground LLM reasoning. Because a graph is too large to provide in full, typical LLM+KG systems preselect a portion, deciding relevance before reasoning begins. Here we train a compact model, Prospector, to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step, seeking evidence in light of what it has already found. Prospector calls a small set of tools one at a time to progressively build its context, and answers with a chain of evidence that can be checked edge by edge against what its tools retrieved from the graph. items.title: ZnO/Ni interface-activated enhancement of spintronic terahertz emission from Ni/Pt bilayers
items.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. However, Ni/Pt bilayers usually exhibit relatively weak THz emission, limiting their use as efficient spintronic emitters. Here, we report an interface-assisted enhancement of THz emission in ZnO/Ni/Pt heterostructures. By placing ZnO underneath Ni while preserving the direct Ni/Pt contact, the THz amplitude is increased by up to approximately 2.8 times compared with the Ni/Pt reference. The enhanced emission reverses polarity with the magnetic field and follows the expected angular dependence of ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. items.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. Donor-bound electron spins in II-VI semiconductors offer an attractive platform for optically active spin qubits because they combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions in a direct-bandgap material with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. items.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
items.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. items.abstract: Cybersecurity education has predominantly focused on software and network security, under the assumption that the underlying hardware is trustworthy. Threats introduced through the global semiconductor supply chain, together with vulnerabilities arising during design and integration, challenge the assumption that hardware can serve as an unquestioned root of trust. Sensor-enabled systems and machine-learning accelerators further expand the hardware attack surface. The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. items.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. items.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
items.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. items.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Time-sensitive neuromorphic architectures require predictable interconnects to preserve precise event timing. Statically scheduled time-division-multiplexed (TDM) circuit-switched networks-on-chip (NoCs) provide deterministic latency at the cost of linear configuration-memory scaling with schedule depth. Furthermore, jointly optimizing task placement, routing, and scheduling creates an intractable combinatorial search space. Existing deployment frameworks also ignore algorithmic axonal delays by forcing immediate spike injections that increase network contention. This paper proposes a hardware-software co-design to address these challenges. ChroNoC is a tableless TDM NoC that embeds precomputed full-grid broadcast trees into combinational logic as a fixed routing substrate. items.title: Nonreciprocal magneto-optic beam steering of thermal emission
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which ties absorptivity to emissivity and places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies and sensing systems. This constraint can be overcome using magneto-optic materials, which exhibit nonreciprocal thermal emission under an applied magnetic field. While the spectral nonreciprocity of magneto-optic devices has been explored theoretically and experimentally, nonreciprocal control over the direction of thermal emission has received far less attention. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate nonreciprocal beam steering of thermal emission, wherein an applied magnetic field lifts the degeneracy between guided modes at +/- kx, enabling asymmetric and tunable directional thermal emission. items.title: Surface Functionalization with Lasers: from Nanostructures to Applications
items.abstract: Pulsed laser sources stand out as remarkable and versatile tools in the growing interdisciplinary field of materials science, offering capabilities for tailoring and customizing materials to meet specific requirements. Their ability to induce different controlled material alterations allows enhancing material properties that might otherwise remain elusive. In essence, laser-induced material modifications encompass a spectrum of transformative processes, ranging from subtle topographical changes in the nano- and microscale, to intricate chemical modifications. Among the challenges to overcome are the creation of approaches that allow tuning the properties of light to optimize interactions on various types of solids, including metals, semiconductors, and dielectrics. Understanding these interactions is paramount towards efficiency increase of the processing techniques. This chapter embarks...

items.title: Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network
items.abstract: \noindent Quantum circuit simulators with hybrid metal-semiconductor dots provide a versatile platform to realize Kondo anyons. These arise at critical points driven by frustrated Kondo screening of dot charge degrees of freedom and have been demonstrated experimentally in linear circuits of one or two dots. Here we study a triangular triple dot device, where geometric frustration gives rise to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_3$ parafermion shared among the three dots. We show that the parafermion can be tunably relocated to any pair of dots by applying gate voltages, and is supported in both the weak-tunneling `Kondo limit' and the strong transmission `quasiballistic' regime. The critical states survive strong coupling to external leads and other dots, establishing the basis for a scalable and reconfigurable network architecture in which non-Abelian excitations can be realized and manipulated.

items.title: When Protection Hurts: A Cytokine Storm Theory of Supply Chain Overreaction
items.abstract: Supply chain resilience research has traditionally viewed defensive actions such as safety stock, backup suppliers, expedited transportation, and emergency sourcing as beneficial. However, disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021 semiconductor shortage, and the Suez Canal blockage highlight how synchronized hoarding, duplicate ordering, and capacity reservation can amplify congestion and operational costs, sometimes worsening the original disruption. Motivated by this observation, we develop a decision-theoretic framework in which Protective Response Intensity (PRI) is an endogenous decision variable. We introduce Response-Induced Loss (RIL) to capture costs generated by defensive actions and characterize a unique optimal response that balances disruption mitigation against self-induced losses. items.title: Optical imaging with only the evanescent fields and without diffraction
items.abstract: We report on a conceptual framework for optical imaging utilizing exclusively evanescent fields, effectively eliminating or attenuating standard optical diffraction. We present the theoretical foundation of this concept based on the decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent fields and homogeneous propagating waves, exploring the explicit conditions required to suppress the latter. By successfully decoupling and removing the homogeneous component, optical tasks, such as sub-diffraction imaging, can be executed solely via evanescent channels, bypassing traditional diffractive limits. We discuss the physical feasibility of this approach and provide concrete examples of how this conjecture can be realized using currently available laboratory and industrial techniques. items.title: Phonon-Dressed Quasiparticles in Epitaxial Scandium Nitride Resolved by Soft X-ray ARPES
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions govern quasiparticle energies, lifetimes, and temperature-dependent band structures in semiconductors. However, direct momentum-resolved experimental evidence of their impact on quasiparticle electronic structure remains scarce, particularly in nitride semiconductors. Here, we present conclusive experimental evidence of electron-phonon interaction-induced quasiparticle renormalization and pronounced spectral broadening in p-type scandium nitride (ScN), using soft x-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. items.title: Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
items.abstract: The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. items.title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. items.abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. items.title: SimSkip: StrongARM-Comparator Similarity Sensing with SAR-Skipping-Aware Training for Analog Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Analog-to-digital conversion dominates the energy and area of analog compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators. This paper presents SimSkip, a successive-approximation-register (SAR) skipping scheme that combines a lightweight StrongARM-comparator similarity detector with SAR-skipping-aware training. When two held voltages are similar, the upper bits of the preceding code are reused to skip SAR comparisons. Detector-induced disturbance extracted from 55-nm CMOS simulations and bit-exact prefix saturation are embedded in the forward pass, and the network learns to tolerate them through quantization-aware training and knowledge distillation. On an ISAAC-based W4A4 WRN-28-10, SimSkip achieves 77.23% CIFAR-100 top-1 accuracy (mean of three seeds) versus 78.4% for the baseline, while reducing SAR comparisons by 48.2% across three hardware-modeled layers. A first-order model estimates a 27.2% net A...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amp...

items.title: A swept-source dual-comb spectrometer on a chip
items.abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) enables high-speed, high-resolution spectroscopy by down-converting optical spectra to the radio-frequency (RF) domain through the interference of two mutually detuned frequency combs. Accurately resolving narrow molecular absorption features requires closely spaced comb lines generated by large laser cavities with long round-trip times, thereby hindering the miniaturization of high-resolution spectrometers. Here, we circumvent this limitation by demonstrating a swept-source dual-comb spectrometer using two unidirectional racetrack semiconductor lasers integrated on the same chip. The traveling-wave frequency combs are generated by strong RF injection at the laser cavity round-trip frequency of 14.3~GHz---otherwise known as quantum walk combs---and are continuously tuned in frequency by varying the laser drive currents. This enables continuous spectral sampli...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q and Small-Mode-Volume Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: Real-Time FPGA-Based Multi-Parameter Feedback Stabilization of a Silicon Double Quantum Dot
items.abstract: Long term operation of semiconductor spin qubits requires active stabilization of quantum dot potentials against low-frequency charge noise. To address this, we demonstrate a gradient-descent feedback approach in a silicon double quantum dot device using high-bandwidth radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry readout and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for digital signal processing. This architecture enables continuous multi-parameter gradient calculation and quick gate voltage updates, significantly increasing the effective feedback bandwidth compared to previous methods relying on slow direct-current transport measurements. By operating with 8 steps per feedback cycle and an integration time of 25.6 $μ$s, this high-speed stabilization scheme maintains better than -6 dB of noise suppression up to 5 kHz, achieving an attenuation of $-7.4 \pm 0.2$ dB at the maximum measured frequency. Th...

items.title: Strain engineering of transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures
items.abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit dark excitons as the energetically lowest states. These are crucial for exciton thermalization and propagation and they dominate low-temperature photoluminescence via the emergence of pronounced phonon sidebands. After a resonant excitation, highly mobile hot dark excitons are formed, which quickly thermalize into an equilibrium distribution. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in strained hBN-encapsulated WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. We demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess ener...

items.title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
items.abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). The proposed architecture is fundamentally robust against m...

items.title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
items.abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. Thus our results shed light on the role of field-bath coupling in the quantum to classical transition of a CMO. The resulting fluctuation-dissipation r...

items.title: Parity-selected charging and noise-correlated work retention in a coupled Si/SiGe double quantum dot battery: theory and experimentally parameterized modeling
items.abstract: We investigate extractable work storage in a capacitively coupled double quantum dot (DQD) quantum battery (QB) subjected to experimentally motivated detuning charge noise. The battery is modeled as two interacting charge qubits with an Ising-type capacitive coupling and is charged by resonant microwave modulation of the tunnel coupling channel. Detuning fluctuations are introduced as classical stochastic processes generated from a band-limited 1/f noise spectrum. For each noise realization, the evolution remains unitary, whereas decoherence and loss of contrast emerge after ensemble averaging. We analyze the total ergotropy, its population and coherent contributions, the energy basis populations, a passive ordering violation diagnostic, and the Jensen-Shannon coherence of the noise-averaged state. The results show that resonant tunnel coupling driving selects a dominant E0 E3 population...

items.title: High-Fidelity Synthetic Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Generation Using Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Data-Limited Semiconductor Metrology
items.abstract: Advanced semiconductor nodes drastically increased demand for Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), yet destructive sample preparation, slow imaging and high costs severely limit the availability of diverse datasets needed for downstream machine learning (ML). Synthetic data generation is becoming essential, but current generative models often miss TEM-specific noise, structural detail, and stochastic variability crucial for evaluation. We present a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) framework for synthetic TEM image generation under extreme data scarcity. A progressive patch-based training strategy scales from low-resolution patches to full images, enabling from-scratch training with only 15 samples. We integrate a custom TrivialAugment adaptation, cross-process domain transfer, classifier guidance, and RePaint-style inpainting, culminating in full-image generation that pr...

items.title: Dispersive mode coupling in $p$-doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
items.abstract: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show that in $p$-doped semiconductors such coupling is strongly enhanced. Moreover, the coupling parameters increase with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The results are applied to Si resonators, where doping is used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.

items.title: Quantum digital simulations of time-domain semiconductor spectroscopy in the semi-classical approximation
items.abstract: We present a digital quantum simulation framework for ultrafast optical spectroscopy of semiconductor materials. The framework is based on Brillouin-zone discretization and is designed as a quantum alternative to classical simulations based on the semiconductor Bloch equations. Its current capabilities include quantum simulations of linear absorption and optical gain, incorporating Lorentzian broadening, finite-temperature band-filling effects, and reduced-dimensionality effects. Comparison with classical simulations of GaAs within the single-particle approximation demonstrates quantitative agreement in the noiseless limit. The inclusion of realistic hardware noise characteristic of NISQ-era quantum computers effectively manifests as an additional source of scattering, resulting in increased spectral broadening. We also show that the linear optical response, including many-body interacti...

items.title: Electrically tunable Crossed Andreev Reflection in Bipolar Magnetic Semiconductors
items.abstract: Crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is a nonlocal quantum transport phenomenon that arises at the interfaces between a superconductor and two spatially separated metals. In this process, an electron incident from one metal combines with another electron originating from the other metal to form a Cooper pair in the SC. In this work, we theoretically investigate the quantum transport properties of a device comprising a central $s$-wave superconductor sandwiched between two bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS) leads. BMS materials possess a unique bandstructure where the conduction and valence bands are fully spin-polarized in opposite directions. By applying independent gate voltages to the two BMS leads, we selectively tune their chemical potentials to configure an antiparallel spin alignment at the Fermi energy.
